{
  "B_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u)*(sqrt((1+u)**2 + r)+(1+u))**2)",
  "C_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u))",
  "derivation": "Let f=1+u and S=sqrt(f*f+r). Inside the full support where chi_r=chi_u=1, the positive root of (z+g)^2=p with z=f and p=f*f+r is g*=S-f. The program requires g=r/2+(r*r*B+u*r*C), so we need r^2*B+u*r*C=g*-r/2. Using S-f=(f*f+r)/(S+f) and r=(S-f)*(S+f), algebra gives g*-r/2 = -r*r/(2*f*(S+f)**2) - u*r/(2*f). Hence B=-1/(2*f*(S+f)**2) and C=-1/(2*f). This generalizes the inherited source u=0 body: at u=0, f=1, B becomes -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2) and C becomes -1/2. The construction cancels the whole signed residual E=(2g+g^2-r)+2*u*g when the two chi factors are one, not merely the pure part. On the closed outer rectangle f lies in [3/4,5/4] and f*f+r is at least 1/16, so the square root and denominator are positive and the bodies are smooth there. This remains a local coefficient-family construction only.",
  "inspect": [],
  "note": "Successor should verify that APPLIED rows with |r|<=1/4 and |u|<=1/8 have residual at rounding scale instead of the prior O(r^2*u+u^2*r) scale, and that ZERO rows remain exactly unchanged. Rows outside the outer rectangle still receive the linear r/2 reference; transition rows with partial chi will have nonzero residual by construction. The square-root domain covers the outer rectangle and a small open neighborhood because (1+u)^2+r>0 and 1+u>0 there; finite numeric behavior is not a full PDE or all-order analytic certificate."
}
